title: Settlement Basis: Agency Service Fee on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
The agency service fee raised on a booking under Air Ticket Fare Brands is the agency service fee of the fare brand held, multiplied by the number of travellers on the booking. It is charged once per traveller on the booking, at the moment the ticket is issued.

**The line it is raised on.** The fee stands as its own line, stated separately from the airline fare and from the taxes and carrier fees.

**Which brand's fee.** The fee follows the fare brand held, not the cabin flown, so a business cabin sold under a saver brand carries the saver brand's fee.

**Worked determination on hypothetical figures.** Take a booking of three travellers whose fare brand carries, hypothetically, an agency service fee of 12.50. The amount raised is 12.50 multiplied by three, that is 37.50, and it is shown apart from the fare and from the taxes and carrier fees.

**Charging in another currency.** Where the traveller elects to be charged in a currency other than the ticketing currency, the conversion markup of the fare brand held is added to the converted total, and the markup is disclosed before the card is taken. Hypothetically, on a converted total of 640.00 with a conversion markup of 4 percent, the markup adds 25.60 and the amount taken is 665.60.

**The fee on a later cancellation.** The fee was not refunded when the traveller later cancelled, the service it pays for having already been performed, and was refunded in full only where the agency itself had cancelled the itinerary in error. That basis is no longer in force. The other clauses of this note stand.

superseded_clauses: The service fee is not refunded when the traveller later cancels, because the service it pays for has already been performed; it is refunded in full only where the agency itself cancelled the itinerary in error.
